stem: During a stakeholder workshop, finance and engineering agree to record the maximum acceptable downtime and the maximum acceptable data loss as two separate numbers pulled from monitoring history. Which TWO metrics are they defining? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: The workload's overall availability percentage, such as 99.99%.
A durability percentage, such as 99.999999999% (eleven nines).
A service quota, such as an EC2 vCPU limit in the recovery Region.

rationale: RTO is precisely the maximum acceptable downtime, expressed as a duration measured from when a disruption starts. RPO is precisely the maximum acceptable data loss, expressed as how far back in time the most recent recoverable data can be. An overall availability percentage summarizes uptime across a whole year rather than stating the maximum downtime or data loss allowed for a single incident, so it is a different, aggregate metric from the two the workshop is defining. A durability percentage such as eleven nines describes how unlikely stored data is to be lost to a storage failure over a year; it is a different, storage-level measure from the workshop's downtime and data-loss numbers, which apply to an incident, not to a year of storage. A service quota such as an EC2 vCPU limit caps how much of a resource an account can use in a Region; it is a capacity ceiling to plan around, not a statement of acceptable downtime or data loss.
